sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **GHG Contribution**: Agriculture accounts for ~10-12% of global anthropogenic GHG emissions, primarily **Methane (CH4)** and **Nitrous Oxide (N2O)**.
• **Land Use Change**: Conversion of forests to croplands leads to **Carbon Sequestration loss** and release of stored soil organic carbon.
• **Nitrogen Cycle Disruption**: Excessive use of **synthetic nitrogenous fertilizers** leads to volatilization and leaching, contributing to N2O emissions.
• **Key Metric**: **Global Warming Potential (GWP)** of N2O is ~273 times that of CO2 over a 100-year horizon, making it a critical focus for climate policy.

items.definition: An approach to guide actions needed to transform and reorient agricultural systems to effectively support development and ensure food security in a changing climate.
The process of capturing and storing atmospheric carbon dioxide in soil (Soil Organic Carbon - SOC) through practices like conservation tillage and agroforestry.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA)**: Focuses on enhancing productivity while mitigating climate risks.
• **System of Rice Intensification (SRI)**: Reduces water usage and methane emissions by avoiding continuous flooding.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Small landholding size, lack of awareness, and high cost of climate-resilient seeds.
• **Solutions**: Promotion of Regenerative Agriculture, Precision Farming, and Bio-fertilizers.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'MAN' (Methane, Ammonia/Nitrogen, Nitrous Oxide).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Methane (Paddy/Livestock), Ammonia/Nitrogen (Fertilizers), Nitrous Oxide (Soil degradation).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Carbon Sequestration' with 'Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)'. Agriculture focuses on biological sequestration, not industrial CCS.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Agro-Ecological Resilience' to describe the shift from input-intensive to knowledge-intensive farming.

keyTakeaways: Agriculture is both a victim and a perpetrator of climate change.
Methane and Nitrous Oxide are the primary GHGs from the sector, not CO2.
Policy shift is moving from 'Yield-centric' to 'Resilience-centric' agriculture.
